discovery: Discovery and spectroscopic characterization of exoplanet atmospheres through transit spectroscopy

nominees.name: David Charbonneau
nominees.affiliation: Harvard University / Center for Astrophysics | Harvard & Smithsonian

subfield: Astrophysics - exoplanet atmospheres and molecular spectroscopy
motivation: In 2000, Charbonneau observed the first transit of an extrasolar planet, HD 209458b. In 2002 he detected the first atmospheric absorption on such a planet. Seager developed the radiative-transfer theory that predicted which atomic and molecular signatures transmission spectra should show, and how to invert them. Tinetti and colleagues then identified water vapour in an exoplanet atmosphere and pioneered retrieval of molecular abundances. Together, this work turned stellar light filtered through distant atmospheres into a quantitative laboratory of molecular physics. It links precise photometry, molecular line data and radiative transfer to the composition of worlds around other stars. With Hubble, Spitzer and now JWST, the method has measured H2O, CO, CO2, CH4 and SO2, revealing photochemistry and C/O ratios that connect planets to the discs where they formed. It opened a new observational window on one of physics' oldest questions: whether our planetary system, and its water, are common.
